extracted.intended_audience: registered practitioners before the USPTO (patent attorneys and agents) and persons granted limited recognition
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules governing USPTO-registered practitioners' contact obligations, administrative suspension/inactivation/resignation, reinstatement requirements, and grounds/procedure for administrative revocation. Covers required filings, timelines, fees, and discipline exposure tied to status changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered practitioner, or person granted limited recognition under § 11.9(b), must notify the OED Director of the postal address for their office, at least one and up to three email addresses where they receive email, and a business telephone number, as well as every change to each of said addresses and telephone number within thirty days of the date of the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to notices of change filed in individual patent applications, the practitioner must separately file written notice of the change of address or telephone number with the OED Director. Attorneys in good standing must provide the identification number associated with each bar membership. The OED Director shall publish a list containing name, postal business addresses, business telephone number, registration or limited recognition number, and registration status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biennial registration statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Biennially, registered practitioners and persons granted limited recognition may be required to file a registration statement with the OED Director for the purpose of ascertaining whether such practitioner desires to remain in an active status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the registration statement or to give any information requested by the OED Director within a specified time limit may subject the practitioner to administrative suspension under paragraph (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative suspension notice and delinquency fee demand
rubrics_metrics.description: When it appears a practitioner has failed to comply with the biennial registration requirement, the OED Director shall publish and send a notice advising of noncompliance, the consequence of administrative suspension if not remedied, and the requirements for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice will be sent to the last postal or email address furnished and shall demand compliance and payment of a delinquency fee set forth in § 1.21(a)(9)(i) within 60 days after the date of such notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to show cause and response timeline for suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If a practitioner fails to comply with the notice demand, the OED Director shall publish and send a notice to show cause why the practitioner should not be administratively suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner has 30 days from the date of the notice to show cause to file a response with the USPTO Director addressing factual and legal bases. The practitioner must serve the OED Director with a copy; the OED Director may file a reply within 10 days. If the USPTO Director finds no genuine issues of material fact regarding notice compliance or failure to pay requisite fees, the USPTO Director shall enter an order administratively suspending the practitioner. Any request for reconsideration must be filed within 20 days of the decision. No stay of suspension is permitted during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline exposure while administratively suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner is subject to investigation and discipline for conduct prior to, during, or after the period he or she was administratively suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An administratively suspended practitioner is prohibited from practicing before the Office in patent matters and must comply with § 11.116. Knowing practice while suspended is itself subject to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative inactivation for USPTO employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any registered practitioner who becomes employed by the Office shall comply with § 11.116 for withdrawal from matters and notify the OED Director in writing of employment on the first day; the name shall be endorsed on the register as administratively inactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon separation from the Office, an administratively inactive practitioner may request reactivation by complying with paragraph (f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative inactivation for judges and judicial officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered practitioners who are judges, full-time court commissioners, U.S. bankruptcy judges, U.S. magistrate judges, or retired judges eligible for temporary assignment and not engaged in practice may request in writing that their names be endorsed as administratively inactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon acceptance, the OED Director endorses the name as administratively inactive. Following separation from the bench, the practitioner may request reactivation under paragraph (f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued applicability of Rules and sanctions during inactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: An administratively inactive practitioner remains subject to the provisions of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and to proceedings and sanctions under §§ 11.19 through 11.58 for conduct that violates a provision of the Rules prior to or during administrative inactivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary inactivation procedure and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Any registered practitioner may voluntarily enter inactive status by filing a written request; upon acceptance the OED Director shall endorse the name as voluntarily inactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A voluntarily inactive practitioner is subject to investigation and discipline for conduct prior to, during, or after inactivation, is prohibited from practicing before the Office in patent cases while inactive, must comply with § 11.116 upon acceptance, and may be restored to active status if not under investigation by filing a written request, a completed registration application with information including moral character and reputation under § 11.7(a)(2)(i), a declaration attesting to reading the most recent revisions of the patent laws and rules, and paying required fees (§ 1.21(a)(7)(iii) and (iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation limitations and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered practitioner or a practitioner recognized under § 11.14(c) may request to resign by notifying the OED Director in writing, unless under investigation under § 11.22, a practitioner against whom probable cause has been found under § 11.23(b), or a respondent in a pending proceeding under §§ 11.24, 11.25, or 11.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon acceptance in writing by the OED Director, the practitioner shall no longer be eligible to practice before the Office in patent matters but must continue to file a change of address for five years so they may be located if information regarding the practitioner's conduct surfaces. The name will be endorsed as resigned and published in the Official Gazette; the practitioner must comply with § 11.116 and remains subject to investigation and discipline for conduct before, during, or after resignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement criteria for administratively suspended practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Any administratively suspended registered practitioner, or person granted limited recognition, may be reinstated provided the practitioner:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (A) is not the subject of a disciplinary investigation or a party to a disciplinary proceeding; (B) has applied for reinstatement on an application form supplied by the OED Director; (C) has demonstrated good moral character and reputation and competence in advising and assisting patent applicants in presentation and prosecution before the Office; (D) has submitted a declaration or affidavit attesting to reading the most recent revisions of the patent laws and rules; (E) has paid the fees in § 1.21(a)(9)(ii); and (F) has paid all applicable delinquency fees in § 1.21(a)(9)(i). If applying more than five years after suspension, the practitioner also must file a petition and provide objective evidence of continued necessary legal qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reactivation requirements for administratively inactive practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner administratively inactivated pursuant to paragraph (c) may be reactivated after employment ceases if the following are filed with the OED Director:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A completed application for reactivation on the form supplied by the OED Director; a data sheet; a signed written undertaking required by § 11.10(b); and the fee in § 1.21(a)(9)(ii). Administratively inactive practitioners separated or ceased judicial employment for five or more years prior to filing must provide objective evidence they continue to possess necessary legal qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement requirements for resigned practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered practitioner endorsed as resigned may be reinstated provided the practitioner:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (A) is not the subject of a disciplinary investigation or a party to a disciplinary proceeding; (B) has applied on an application form supplied by the OED Director; (C) has demonstrated good moral character and reputation and competence in advising and assisting patent applicants; (D) has submitted a declaration attesting to reading the most recent revisions of the patent laws and rules; (E) has paid the fees in § 1.21(a)(9)(ii); and (F) has paid all applicable delinquency fees in § 1.21(a)(9)(i). Resigned practitioners applying more than five years after resignation also must file a petition and provide objective evidence of continued necessary legal qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative revocation grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director may revoke an individual's registration or limited recognition if: (i) the registration or limited recognition was issued through mistake or inadvertence, or (ii) the individual's application for registration or limited recognition contains materially false information or omits material information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative revocation procedure and response timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever it appears grounds for revocation exist, the OED Director shall issue a notice to show cause served in the manner described in § 11.35, stating the grounds and filing a copy with the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The individual has 30 days after service to file a response with the USPTO Director addressing factual or legal bases why registration should not be revoked and must serve a copy on the OED Director. The OED Director may file a reply within 10 days. If the USPTO Director finds no genuine issues of material fact regarding notice compliance or grounds, the USPTO Director shall enter an order revoking the registration; otherwise the notice will be dismissed. An oral hearing will not be granted unless ordered by the USPTO Director upon finding it necessary. Any request for reconsideration of the USPTO Director's decision must be filed within 20 days. Nothing permits seeking a stay of the revocation during review of the final decision.
